$comment: The releases this project measures itself against, and the facts that identify them.
Read by the `Reference releases are intact` step in release-dmg.yml, which fails the
build if any of these tags disappears or moves to a different commit.
GitHub-side tag protection became available when this repository was made public on
2026-08-17 — rulesets need Pro or a public repository, and it is now the latter. This
check is kept alongside rather than replaced by one: a ruleset can stop a tag being
deleted, but it does not record which commit the tag is supposed to point at, nor the
digest of the artifact that was published from it. Those are the facts a fallback point
is actually made of, and they live here.
Three references. v1.0.5 is the floor, v1.0.9 closes the 1.x line, and v2.5.2 is the
current release, made a reference on 2026-09-04 by the owner's decision. A release
cannot record itself — the commit it names is the commit that carries it, and no file
can contain its own hash — so each entry here is added by the commit after the release
it describes.
v2.5.2 replaced v2.5.1, which was withdrawn on 2026-09-04 — release, tag and DMG. A
reference cannot be re-cut, so the work that followed it took a number of its own, and
keeping the list at three meant retiring the release it replaced rather than letting
both stand. The same happened to v2.5.0 on 2026-09-01 and to v2.1.0 through v2.4.0 on
2026-08-30, so the 2.x line is still represented by its head alone. What that costs is
named rather than hidden: a fault introduced this week is no longer bracketed from
below by anything nearer than v1.0.9. The list is kept at three deliberately; the next
reference worth adding is the first 2.x state after this one that is worth falling back
to, and adding it is a decision rather than a consequence of publishing.
Adding or changing any value below is a deliberate act and shows up in the diff as one.

references.why: First release of the numbering that survives; everything before it was withdrawn.
The second reference: credits the corpus authors, bounds a download that had nothing but the disk to stop it, and is the recent state to fall back to rather than the floor.

The current release and the third reference: the first version in which what a reader installs is the application with a window rather than an image built from the console crate. The bundle is `Aruna.app`, the identifier is the product's rather than a shell suffix, the shell's version equals the core's and a test compares the two manifests, the signature is ad hoc stated in the configuration itself, and the minimum system version is the macOS 13 the program actually targets instead of Tauri's 10.13 default. It replaced v2.5.1, withdrawn the same day: that release was the reference this one is cut from, and a reference cannot be re-cut, so the work took a number of its own and the old reference was retired rather than left standing beside it.
